title: Equations and Calculations
description: Balancing equations, using moles and reading symbol equations.
hero_image_caption: Every chemical reaction is governed by a precise bookkeeping of atoms — nothing created, nothing destroyed.
content_html:
Conservation of Mass

In any chemical reaction, atoms are neither created nor destroyed — they are simply rearranged. This is the law of conservation of mass. It means a correctly written symbol equation must have the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the arrow. An equation with unequal atom counts is unbalanced and does not represent a real reaction.

Key Fact

In a chemical reaction, total mass is conserved. A balanced symbol equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides of the arrow. You balance equations by adding large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas — never by changing the subscripts inside a formula.

Balancing Symbol Equations

To balance a symbol equation, count the atoms on each side and adjust the large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas until both sides match. You must never change the subscripts inside a formula (that would change the substance itself). Work through one element at a time, leaving hydrogen and oxygen until last when they appear in water or acids.

Balance the equation for the combustion of propane: \(C_3H_8 + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + H_2O\)

Step 1: Count carbons. Left: 3; Right: 1. Put a 3 in front of \(CO_2\):
\(C_3H_8 + O_2 \rightarrow 3CO_2 + H_2O\)

Step 2: Count hydrogens. Left: 8; Right: 2. Put a 4 in front of \(H_2O\):
\(C_3H_8 + O_2 \rightarrow 3CO_2 + 4H_2O\)

Step 3: Count oxygens. Right: 3×2 + 4×1 = 10. Left needs 5 \(O_2\):
\(C_3H_8 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 3CO_2 + 4H_2O\)

Step 4: Check all atoms. C: 3=3 ✓ H: 8=8 ✓ O: 10=10 ✓. The equation is balanced.

State symbols can be added in brackets after each formula to show the physical state: (s) = solid, (l) = liquid, (g) = gas, (aq) = aqueous (dissolved in water). For example: \(Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow MgCl_2(aq) + H_2(g)\)

Relative Formula Mass

The relative formula mass (\(M_r\)) of a compound is calculated by adding together the relative atomic masses (\(A_r\)) of all the atoms shown in its formula. For example, for water (\(H_2O\)):

$$M_r(H_2O) = 2 \times A_r(H) + 1 \times A_r(O) = 2 \times 1 + 16 = 18$$

For sulfuric acid (\(H_2SO_4\)): \(M_r = 2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 98\). You need the periodic table to look up \(A_r\) values. The relative formula mass tells you the mass of one formula unit in atomic mass units, and is numerically equal to the mass of one mole in grams.

Key Fact

Relative formula mass (Mr): add up the Ar of every atom in the formula, accounting for subscripts. Mr of CaCO₃ = 40 + 12 + 3×16 = 100. No units — it is a ratio relative to ¹²C.

The Mole

Atoms and molecules are far too small to count individually, so chemists use the mole as a counting unit. One mole of any substance contains the same enormous number of particles — approximately \(6.02 \times 10^{23}\) — known as Avogadro's constant. The genius of the mole is that one mole of an element has a mass in grams exactly equal to its relative atomic mass.

The key equation linking moles, mass, and molar mass is:

$$\text{number of moles} = \frac{\text{mass (g)}}{\text{molar mass (g/mol)}}$$

Rearranged: mass = moles × molar mass, or molar mass = mass ÷ moles.

Worked example: How many moles are in 44 g of carbon dioxide (\(CO_2\), \(M_r = 44\))?
Moles = 44 ÷ 44 = 1 mol.

Second example: What mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH, \(M_r = 40\)) is needed to make 0.5 mol?
Mass = 0.5 × 40 = 20 g.

Always show your working in full and include units at every step — examiners deduct marks for missing units on multi-step calculations.

Using Equations to Calculate Reacting Masses

A balanced symbol equation shows the molar ratios of reactants and products — the large numbers (coefficients) tell you how many moles of each substance react. Combined with molar masses, this allows calculation of the mass of any reactant or product from a known mass of another.

Calculate the mass of iron produced when 160 g of iron(III) oxide (\(Fe_2O_3\)) reacts with excess carbon:
\(2Fe_2O_3 + 3C \rightarrow 4Fe + 3CO_2\)

Step 1: Find \(M_r\) of \(Fe_2O_3\): \(2 \times 56 + 3 \times 16 = 160\) g/mol.

Step 2: Calculate moles of \(Fe_2O_3\): \(\frac{160}{160} = 1 \text{ mol}\).

Step 3: Use the molar ratio. From the equation, 2 mol \(Fe_2O_3\) → 4 mol Fe, so 1 mol \(Fe_2O_3\) → 2 mol Fe.

Step 4: Convert moles of Fe to mass: \(2 \times 56 = \mathbf{112 \text{ g}}\).

Key Fact

Reacting mass calculation (Higher): (1) write balanced equation, (2) calculate Mr of known substance and find moles, (3) use molar ratio from equation to find moles of unknown substance, (4) convert moles to mass. Always show every step and include units.
exam_tip_html: For balancing equations, always check every element after your final balance — it is easy to miss an oxygen. For mole calculations at Higher Tier, show every step clearly: molar mass calculation, moles calculation, ratio step, final mass. Examiners award marks for correct method even if the final answer is wrong due to an arithmetic slip. Common error: forgetting to multiply by the ratio from the balanced equation before converting back to mass.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Conservation of mass means balanced equations must have identical atom counts on both sides. Balance by adjusting coefficients, never subscripts.
  • Relative formula mass (Mr) is the sum of all relative atomic masses in a formula. One mole of a substance has a mass in grams equal to its Mr.
  • Avogadro's constant (≈ 6.02 × 10²³) is the number of particles in one mole. Higher Tier: moles = mass ÷ molar mass; use molar ratios from balanced equations to calculate reacting masses.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following equations is correctly balanced?
A) H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
B) 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
C) H₂ + O → H₂O
D) H₂ + 2O → 2H₂O

Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃.
(Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
Describe the steps a student should follow to balance the symbol equation for the reaction between magnesium and hydrochloric acid: Mg + HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
practice_questions.marks: Count Mg: 1=1, balanced [1]; count Cl: right has 2, so put 2 in front of HCl [1]; check H: left has 2 (from 2HCl), right has 2 (H₂) — balanced. Final equation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ [1].

practice_questions.text:
Calculate the mass of water produced when 80 g of methane (CH₄) undergoes complete combustion.
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
(Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
Show all your working.
practice_questions.marks: Mr of CH₄ = 12 + 4(1) = 16 g/mol [1]; moles of CH₄ = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 mol [1]; ratio 1:2 so moles of H₂O = 10 mol [1]; mass of H₂O = 10 × 18 = 180 g [1].

practice_questions.text: A scientist finds that when 2.4 g of magnesium burns in air, a white solid with a mass greater than 2.4 g is produced. A student claims this contradicts the law of conservation of mass. Evaluate whether the student is correct, using your knowledge of conservation of mass and what happens during combustion.
practice_questions.marks: StudyVault Mastering: the student is incorrect [1]; conservation of mass applies to all atoms involved in the reaction, including from the air [1]; magnesium reacts with oxygen from the air to form magnesium oxide [1]; the mass of oxygen from the air is added to the magnesium [1]; total mass of reactants (Mg + O₂) equals total mass of product (MgO) [1]. Secure: four points. Developing: identifies product is heavier and involves oxygen but does not fully apply conservation.

practice_questions.text:
Zinc oxide reacts with carbon to produce zinc and carbon dioxide:
2ZnO + C → 2Zn + CO₂
(Ar: Zn = 65, O = 16, C = 12)
Calculate the mass of zinc produced from 18.1 g of zinc oxide, and explain what the molar ratio in the equation tells you about the reaction.
practice_questions.marks: StudyVault Mastering: Mr ZnO = 65 + 16 = 81 g/mol [1]; moles ZnO = 18.1 ÷ 81 = 0.223 mol [1]; ratio 2:2 so moles Zn = 0.223 mol [1]; mass Zn = 0.223 × 65 = 14.5 g [1]; explanation: coefficients show the relative number of moles of each substance reacting [1]; 2 mol ZnO reacts with 1 mol C to give 2 mol Zn and 1 mol CO₂ — this fixed ratio cannot be changed [1]. Secure: four calculation marks. Developing: correct Mr and moles only.

knowledge_checks.q: What does the law of conservation of mass state?
options: The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
Atoms are created during chemical reactions

knowledge_checks.q: How do you balance a symbol equation?
options: Add large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas
Remove atoms from the product side
Change the chemical formulas of the reactants

knowledge_checks.q: The relative formula mass (Mr) of water (H₂O)? (Ar: H=1, O=16) is _____
One mole of carbon (Ar = 12) has a mass of ___.: _____

knowledge_checks.instruction: Match each term or concept to its correct description
left: the law of conservation of mass state
One mole of carbon (Ar = 12) has a mass of ___.
right: The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
Add large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas

flashcard_questions.q: What is the law of conservation of mass?
flashcard_questions.a: The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction, because atoms are neither created nor destroyed.

flashcard_questions.q: How do you calculate relative formula mass (Mr)?
flashcard_questions.a: Add together the relative atomic masses of all atoms in the chemical formula, accounting for any subscripts.
A unit of amount of substance. One mole contains approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles and has a mass in grams equal to the relative formula mass.
The number of particles in one mole of any substance, approximately 6.02 × 10²³.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for calculating the number of moles from mass?
flashcard_questions.a: Number of moles = mass (g) ÷ molar mass (g/mol).

flashcard_questions.q: What do state symbols in a chemical equation tell you?
flashcard_questions.a: The physical state of each substance: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) dissolved in water.

flashcard_questions.q: In a balanced equation, what do the large numbers in front of formulas represent?
flashcard_questions.a: Coefficients — they show the relative number of moles of each substance involved in the reaction.

glossary_terms.definition: The principle that the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction, because atoms are neither created nor destroyed.
An equation using chemical symbols and formulas to show the reactants and products of a reaction and their relative amounts.
The sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a compound's formula. Symbol: Mr. It has no units.
The unit of amount of substance in chemistry. One mole contains approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles and has a mass in grams equal to the relative formula mass.
The number of particles in one mole of any substance, approximately 6.02 × 10²³.
The mass of one mole of a substance in grams per mole (g/mol), numerically equal to the relative formula mass.
The large number placed in front of a formula in a balanced chemical equation to show the relative number of moles of that substance involved in the reaction.
